title: NeuroFlow CFD — Case Study
summary: Why the architecture looks like it does, not just what was built.
problem: Rupture-risk assessment does not scale as a manual, specialist-only process.
constraints: Clinical DICOM data is noisy; the pipeline had to tolerate imaging artifacts without silently producing bad meshes.
technicalDecisions: Validating mesh quality before simulation, rather than after a solver crash, was the single highest-leverage decision in the whole pipeline.
challenges: Non-manifold geometry from imaging artifacts crashed the CFD solver in ways that were hard to distinguish from genuine simulation failures.
lessonsLearned: Catch data-quality problems as early in the pipeline as possible — every stage they slip past multiplies the cost of diagnosing them.

body.raw: The Project page is the artifact record. This page is the decision log — why the pipeline is shaped the way it is, not just what it does.
